concept.title: Tables in the Visual Editor
concept.shortdesc: Insert and edit CALS and simple tables on the page: rows, columns, merged cells and column widths, with the table markup kept consistent for you.

section.title: Table Commands
section.p: Table in the toolbar inserts a CALS table with a header row and column specifications. With the cursor in a cell, the same menu — and Table in the right-click menu — edits the table:

strow.stentry: A row with one cell per free column; a cell spanning rows across the new row grows (morerows)
The row; spans into it shrink, a span starting in it moves to the next row
A cell in every row, a new <colspec>, and @cols + 1; a span across the new column widens
The cells of the column, its colspec, and @cols − 1
One cell spanning both (namest/nameend or morerows), contents joined
A merged cell becomes one cell per slot again
The first body row becomes the header row (thead), or back

section.p: Tab and Shift+Tab move to the next and previous cell; Tab in the last cell adds a row. Simple tables (simpletable) work the same way, with @relcolwidth following column changes. A command that would break the table is not offered. Rows and cells a command does not change are written back as they were.

section.title: Column Widths
section.p: Tables show their column widths (colspec/@colwidth, or a simple table's @relcolwidth). Drag the border between two columns to move width from one to the other: a guide shows the two new widths; release to set them (Escape cancels, Ctrl+Z undoes).

image.alt: A three-column table of settings; the border between the first two columns is being dragged and a guide shows the new widths 41* and 14*.

ul.li: Proportional widths are written as whole numbers out of 100 (30*, 70*); a table whose proportions do not add up to 100 has them rewritten that way the first time.
A CALS table without colspecs gets them.
